paths.name: Filtration vs. noise-driven adherence
paths.what_opens: Optimize for hours-actually-run under real noise tolerance, not peak lab CADR.

test.text: Falsified when one design point achieves RP-01's measured primary-room particulate reduction at a sound level that removes noise as a named reason for running the device less (RP-05) - both halves are stored, quantified findings.

source_quotes.RP-01.found: PM2.5/PM10 fell 78.8%/63.9% in the primary room and 57.9%/60.4% in a secondary room during the filter condition vs. sham.
source_quotes.RP-05.establishes: In this small pilot, noise was a real, named reason people ran the device less than intended.

paths.detail: Higher measured filtration performance generally requires longer runtime, but RP-05 found noise was a named reason real users under-ran DIY cleaners - a device that filters best in the lab may filter worst in practice if nobody keeps it on.

supporting_evidence.title: Self-reported health impacts of do-it-yourself air cleaner use in a smoke-impacted community
supporting_evidence.found: No association was found between DIY air-cleaner usage and self-reported symptoms; usage itself was low, and loud operating noise was cited as a barrier to use.
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That air cleaners don't help symptoms in general - the sample was too small and usage too inconsistent to draw a causal conclusion either way.

supporting_evidence.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Portable Air Cleaners in Reducing Home Particulate Matter Concentrations
supporting_evidence.found: PM2.5/PM10 fell 78.8%/63.9% in the primary room and 57.9%/60.4% in a secondary room during the filter condition vs. sham.
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That secondary-room reduction generalizes to homes without central air handling, or to non-COVID-positive households.

supporting_evidence.title: Reduction of personal PM2.5 exposure via indoor air filtration systems in Detroit: an intervention study
supporting_evidence.found: True-HEPA cut personal PM2.5 exposure 53% and indoor concentration 60%; a cheaper HEPA-type filter still cut exposure 31% and concentration 52%.
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That the gap between true-HEPA and HEPA-type performance is negligible for all pollutant sizes or health outcomes.

paths.name: Constant vs. automatic operation
paths.what_opens: Ship the trade-off as a visible, explainable choice rather than a single hidden factory default.

test.text: Falsified when an auto-mode arm reaches the lower bound of RP-07's constant-mode reduction interval while keeping auto's runtime/noise advantage - the two stored confidence intervals would then overlap and the trade-off dissolves.

source_quotes.RP-07.found: Constant operation cut weekly mean PM2.5 by 66% (95% CI 59-72%); auto operation cut it by 40% (95% CI 27-50%) but sharply reduced runtime.

paths.detail: RP-07's own three-arm trial shows constant operation removes more PM2.5 (66%) than auto mode (40%), but auto mode sharply cuts runtime/noise/energy - there is no operating mode that wins on both axes at once.

supporting_evidence.title: The impact of portable air cleaners on indoor particulate matter concentrations and perceptions of indoor air quality: a randomized crossover trial in three multifamily buildings
supporting_evidence.found: Constant operation cut weekly mean PM2.5 by 66% (95% CI 59-72%); auto operation cut it by 40% (95% CI 27-50%) but sharply reduced runtime.
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That one control strategy (always-constant or always-auto) is optimal for every home - the paper explicitly says a universal strategy may not fit.

paths.detail: RP-07 explicitly reports a discrepancy between theoretical CADR-based sizing and measured performance; RP-01 shows lab-style single-room performance doesn't fully carry to a second room; RP-06 shows raw real-home averages can even look wrong unless corrected for source strength.

paths.name: More sensing vs. sensor trust
paths.what_opens: A 'smart' control claim needs an honest confidence signal, not just a raw sensor number.

test.text: Challenged when a consumer air-quality sensor passes a formal regulatory validation standard - RP-09's stored finding is that most currently do not.

source_quotes.RP-09.found: Many low-cost sensors correlate well with reference instruments under controlled conditions, but performance varies significantly with humidity, temperature, and pollutant source; most devices don't yet meet formal regulatory validation standards.

paths.detail: RP-09's systematic review and RP-10's co-location study both find that consumer-grade sensors can be precise (track relative change well) while still being inaccurate (wrong absolute value) - especially as humidity, temperature and pollutant source vary.
paths.reclassification_why: RP-09 and RP-10 agree - the signals layer classifies sensor_trust as CONVERGING with 2 independent studies. Agreeing evidence is not a tension; 'more sensing implies more trust' is a category belief the evidence already challenges.

supporting_evidence.title: Low-cost sensors for indoor air quality monitoring: A systematic review of accuracy, applications, and limitations
supporting_evidence.found: Many low-cost sensors correlate well with reference instruments under controlled conditions, but performance varies significantly with humidity, temperature, and pollutant source; most devices don't yet meet formal regulatory validation standards.
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That any specific consumer purifier's onboard sensor is accurate enough to safely drive fully autonomous decisions in all conditions.

supporting_evidence.title: Validating the performance of low-cost IAQ sensors through co-location
supporting_evidence.found: One consumer sensor tracked relative CO2/PM changes well (higher correlation) but showed higher bias/RMSE (lower absolute accuracy) than the reference; averaging over longer intervals improved but did not eliminate the gap.
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That either tested sensor is reliable enough for uncalibrated absolute-concentration claims without in-situ calibration.

unknowns.text: Both studies test PM2.5/CO2 sensors specifically; may not generalize to other pollutant sensors (e.g. VOC).

paths.name: Room-level cleaning vs. spatial/floor sources
paths.what_opens: Spatial-source modeling should not assume deposited particles stay deposited, but no placement claim follows from this evidence alone.

test.text: Challenged only by a study that tests purifier placement against floor-level resuspension - RP-04's own record states no placement was tested. The honest answer today is that the deciding test does not exist yet.

source_quotes.RP-04.does_not_establish: That a floor-level or mobile purifier would outperform a conventional room-level purifier - this study did not test any purifier placement.

paths.detail: RP-04 shows ordinary walking measurably resuspends floor-deposited particles back into room air - a real spatial source the standard stationary-room-purifier model does not directly address. NOT ESTABLISHED: that a floor-level or mobile purifier would outperform a conventional purifier - RP-04 tested no purifier placement at all.
paths.reclassification_why: Single source (RP-04), and the record's own statement says the alternative was never tested ('RP-04 tested no purifier placement at all') - an open question, not contested evidence.

supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That a floor-level or mobile purifier would outperform a conventional room-level purifier - this study did not test any purifier placement.

paths.name: Pollutant reduction vs. clinical outcome certainty
paths.what_opens: Never assert a health-outcome claim from PM-reduction evidence alone; RP-08's result needs independent replication before being treated as settled.

test.text: Resolved when an independent replication of RP-08 reproduces its clinical effect in a cohort whose particulate reduction matches RP-03's measured range - RP-08's own record names independent replication as the missing step. A failed replication resolves it the other way.

source_quotes.RP-08.found: The active group gained +2.2 Asthma Control Test points and +27.7% symptom-free days versus placebo, alongside a 29.6 microg/m3 PM2.5 drop (all p<=0.004).
source_quotes.RP-08.does_not_establish: That this specific effect size generalizes beyond this single trial - treat as a candidate finding requiring independent replication before treating as settled.
source_quotes.RP-03.found: HEPA homes had 60% lower sleeping-area and 42% lower living-area PM2.5 at one year; ammonia reductions were not observed.

paths.detail: RP-08 found a measurable asthma-control benefit (ACT score, symptom-free days) from real HEPA filtration in one RCT; RP-03 (ammonia) and RP-05 (self-reported symptoms) found PM/exposure changes did NOT correspond to the specific outcomes they measured. The real literature is not unanimous that pollutant reduction equals a felt health benefit.

supporting_evidence.title: Indoor environmental health and asthma relief: findings from a longitudinal HEPA filter trial
supporting_evidence.found: The active group gained +2.2 Asthma Control Test points and +27.7% symptom-free days versus placebo, alongside a 29.6 microg/m3 PM2.5 drop (all p<=0.004).
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That this specific effect size generalizes beyond this single trial - treat as a candidate finding requiring independent replication before treating as settled.

supporting_evidence.title: Effectiveness of portable HEPA air cleaners on reducing indoor PM2.5 and NH3 in an agricultural cohort of children with asthma: A randomized intervention trial
supporting_evidence.found: HEPA homes had 60% lower sleeping-area and 42% lower living-area PM2.5 at one year; ammonia reductions were not observed.
supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That reduced PM2.5 translated into fewer asthma symptoms - no clinical/symptom endpoint was reported in this result.

supporting_evidence.title: Self-reported health impacts of do-it-yourself air cleaner use in a smoke-impacted community

supporting_evidence.does_not_establish: That air cleaners don't help symptoms in general - the sample was too small and usage too inconsistent to draw a causal conclusion either way.

CONVERGENCE.name: Noise / motor sound (weak real signal)
CONVERGENCE.detail: Independent evidence families agree: Motor/fan noise is a recurring complaint, now backed by peer-reviewed evidence it drives real under-use.

CONVERGENCE.name: Ozone / smell / irritation (weak real signal)
CONVERGENCE.detail: Independent evidence families agree: Ozone/smell/irritation complaints converge with real regulatory guidance on ozone safety limits.

CONVERGENCE.name: Perceived value / does it actually clean the air
CONVERGENCE.detail: Independent evidence families agree: Whether it 'actually cleans the air' is backed by four real peer-reviewed effectiveness trials.

CONVERGENCE.name: Sensor precision != sensor accuracy
CONVERGENCE.detail: Independent evidence families agree: Consumer-grade IAQ sensors can track relative change well while reporting materially wrong absolute numbers - a 'smart' claim needs a trust qualifier, not just a reading.

TENSION.name: Filtration vs. noise-driven adherence
TENSION.detail: Higher measured filtration performance generally requires longer runtime, but RP-05 found noise was a named reason real users under-ran DIY cleaners - a device that filters best in the lab may filter worst in practice if nobody keeps it on.

TENSION.name: Constant vs. automatic operation
TENSION.detail: RP-07's own three-arm trial shows constant operation removes more PM2.5 (66%) than auto mode (40%), but auto mode sharply cuts runtime/noise/energy - there is no operating mode that wins on both axes at once.

TENSION.name: CADR theory vs. real-home performance
TENSION.detail: RP-07 explicitly reports a discrepancy between theoretical CADR-based sizing and measured performance; RP-01 shows lab-style single-room performance doesn't fully carry to a second room; RP-06 shows raw real-home averages can even look wrong unless corrected for source strength.

TENSION.name: Pollutant reduction vs. clinical outcome certainty
TENSION.detail: RP-08 found a measurable asthma-control benefit (ACT score, symptom-free days) from real HEPA filtration in one RCT; RP-03 (ammonia) and RP-05 (self-reported symptoms) found PM/exposure changes did NOT correspond to the specific outcomes they measured. The real literature is not unanimous that pollutant reduction equals a felt health benefit.

CONTRADICTION.name: Filtration-to-health-benefit evidence is genuinely split
CONTRADICTION.detail: Real evidence genuinely disagrees: One real RCT (RP-08) found a significant asthma-control benefit from HEPA filtration; two other real studies (RP-03, RP-05) measuring related pollutants/symptoms found no such association.

ASSUMPTION.detail: 170 of 237 real corpus products (72%) are classified standard_purifier - a single dedicated appliance is still the dominant real architecture.

ASSUMPTION.detail: ENERGY STAR and AHAM certification (TC-R02, TC-R03) both center CADR as the official performance metric.

ASSUMPTION.detail: Standard purifier control panels default to a fixed or continuous mode; only 15 of 237 products are classified connected, and 8 adaptive.

ASSUMPTION.name: More sensing vs. sensor trust
ASSUMPTION.detail: RP-09's systematic review and RP-10's co-location study both find that consumer-grade sensors can be precise (track relative change well) while still being inaccurate (wrong absolute value) - especially as humidity, temperature and pollutant source vary. (reclassified from TENSION: RP-09 and RP-10 agree - the signals layer classifies sensor_trust as CONVERGING with 2 independent studies. Agreeing evidence is not a tension; 'more sensing implies more trust' is a category belief the evidence already challenges.)

ASSUMPTION.detail: RP-04 shows ordinary walking measurably resuspends floor-deposited particles back into room air - a real spatial source the standard stationary-room-purifier model does not directly address. NOT ESTABLISHED: that a floor-level or mobile purifier would outperform a conventional purifier - RP-04 tested no purifier placement at all.
